    15→   between evalCNF and cnfSharesFactor

    17→   time = tape length

    19→   polynomial walk complexity
    20→4. **NDM Entropy Walk** — conditional entropy accumulated inside the
    21→   machine
    22→5. **NDM Circuit Evaluation** — circuit SAT via address space
    23→
    24→## Main definitions
    25→
    26→* `ReadHead` — the state of a sequential tape reader.
    27→* `timeComplexity` — time cost of a program in the computation model.
    28→* `literalAddress` / `literalAddressPath` — polarity-encoded literal
    29→  addresses.
    30→* `ndmAddressWalk` / `ndmWalkComplexity` — endpoint-free clause-by-clause
    31→  address recording.
    32→* `NDMEntropyWalkState` / `ndmEntropyWalk` — conditional entropy
    33→  accumulated inside the machine.
    34→* `literalAddressesFromAssignment` — the k addresses selected by an
    35→  assignment.
    36→* `ndmCircuitEval` — circuit evaluation in address space.
    37→
    38→## Main results
    39→
    40→* `timeComplexity_eq_length` — time complexity equals tape length.
    41→* `ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF` — the NDM circuit IS evalCNF.
    42→* `ndmEntropyWalk_determines_sat` — entropy walk determines SAT.
    43→* `ndmWalkComplexity_polynomial` — walk cost is polynomial.
    44→* `ndmCircuit_entropy_bridge` — circuit evaluation matches entropy walk.
    45→* `ndmCircuit_sat_iff` — SAT iff exists assignment where circuit accepts.
    46→-/
    47→
    48→open InformationTheory InformationTheory.EntropyNat
    49→
    50→namespace InformationTheory
    51→
    52→-- Decomposition definitions (chosenLiteral, cnfSharesFactor, conditional entropy, etc.)
    53→-- are imported from InformationTheory.Complexity.Decomposition
    54→
    55→/-!
    56→## The Read Head Model
    57→
    58→A `ReadHead` processes a tape bit by bit. At each step, the head
    59→reads one bit and advances. The number of steps taken is provably
    60→equal to the tape length.
    61→-/
    62→
    63→/--
    64→The state of a sequential tape reader at any point during execution.
    65→`remaining` is the unread portion of the tape; `steps` counts how
    66→many bits have been read so far.
    67→-/
    68→structure ReadHead where
    69→  remaining : ComputerTape
    70→  steps     : ℕ
    71→
    72→/--
    73→Initialize the read head at the beginning of a tape. Zero steps
    74→taken.
    75→-/
    76→def ReadHead.init (tape : ComputerTape) : ReadHead :=
    77→  { remaining := tape, steps := 0 }
    78→
    79→/--
    80→One step of execution: read one bit from the tape head, advance,
    81→increment the step counter. Returns `none` if the tape is exhausted.
    82→-/
    83→def ReadHead.step (head : ReadHead) :
    84→    Option (Bool × ReadHead) :=
    85→  match head.remaining with
    86→  | [] => none
    87→  | bit :: rest =>
    88→    some (bit, { remaining := rest,
    89→                 steps := head.steps + 1 })
    90→
    91→/--
    92→Run the read head to completion: process every bit on the tape
    93→sequentially. Returns the final state (empty tape, all steps
    94→counted).
    95→-/
    96→def ReadHead.run : ReadHead → ReadHead
    97→  | { remaining := [], steps := s } =>
    98→    { remaining := [], steps := s }
    99→  | { remaining := _ :: rest, steps := s } =>
   100→      ReadHead.run { remaining := rest, steps := s + 1 }
   101→termination_by head => head.remaining.length
   102→
   103→/--
   104→**The time complexity of a program in the computation model**: the number
   105→of sequential read steps required to process the entire tape.
   106→
   107→This is defined as the step count after running the read head to
   108→completion.
   109→-/
   110→def timeComplexity (prog : ComputerProgram) : ℕ :=
   111→  (ReadHead.init prog |>.run).steps
   112→
   113→/-!
   114→### Core Theorems: Time Complexity = Tape Length
   115→-/
   116→
   117→/--
   118→After running the read head on a tape, the remaining tape is empty.
   119→Every bit has been processed.
   120→-/
   121→theorem ReadHead.run_exhausts (head : ReadHead) :
   122→    (head.run).remaining = [] := by
   123→  induction head using ReadHead.run.induct with
   124→  | case1 s => simp [ReadHead.run]
   125→  | case2 bit rest s ih => simp [ReadHead.run]; exact ih
   126→
   127→/--
   128→The step count after running equals the initial steps plus the tape
   129→length. This is the key lemma: every bit contributes exactly one
   130→step.
   131→-/
   132→theorem ReadHead.run_steps (head : ReadHead) :
   133→    (head.run).steps =
   134→      head.steps + head.remaining.length := by
   135→  induction head using ReadHead.run.induct with
   136→  | case1 s => simp [ReadHead.run]
   137→  | case2 bit rest s ih =>
   138→    simp [ReadHead.run]
   139→    rw [ih]
   140→    simp [List.length_cons]
   141→    omega
   142→
   143→/--
   144→**Time complexity equals tape length.**
   145→
   146→For any `ComputerProgram`, the time complexity (number of
   147→sequential read operations) is exactly the tape length. Each bit
   148→costs one step. No free memory access. No loops. No revisits.
   149→
   150→This is the formal statement that in the computation model,
   151→**program complexity = time complexity = information content**.
   152→
   153→Combined with:
   154→- RECT/IRECT: information content = program complexity
   155→- Shannon SCT: optimal code length = entropy for IID source
   156→- Rota: log is the unique entropy function
   157→- LFTA: primes are perfect Shannon coders
   158→
   159→The chain is:
   160→time complexity = tape length = information content = entropy.
   161→-/
   162→theorem timeComplexity_eq_length
   163→    (prog : ComputerProgram) :
   164→    timeComplexity prog = prog.length := by
   165→  simp [timeComplexity, ReadHead.init, ReadHead.run_steps]
   166→
   167→/--
   168→Time complexity of the empty program is zero.
   169→-/
   170→@[simp] theorem timeComplexity_nil :
   171→    timeComplexity ([] : ComputerProgram) = 0 := by
   172→  simp [timeComplexity_eq_length]
   173→
   174→/--
   175→Time complexity of a single instruction is one.
   176→-/
   177→@[simp] theorem timeComplexity_singleton (b : Bool) :
   178→    timeComplexity [b] = 1 := by
   179→  simp [timeComplexity_eq_length]
   180→
   181→/-! ## Chain 1 declarations — NDM address walk, entropy
   182→    walk, circuit eval
   183→
   184→The remaining declarations below ARE part of the P=NP proof chain
   185→(Chain 1). They are directly imported by `PPNP.lean`:
   186→`literalAddress`, `literalAddressPath`, `ndmAddressWalk`,
   187→`ndmWalkComplexity`, `NDMEntropyWalkState`, `ndmEntropyWalk`,
   188→`ndmEntropyWalk_*` theorems, `ndmCircuitEval`,
   189→`ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF`, `ndmCircuit_entropy_bridge`,
   190→`ndmCircuit_sat_iff`, `ndmCircuit_cost_polynomial`, and
   191→`ndmWalkComplexity_polynomial`.
   192→-/
   193→
   194→/-! ## NDM Address-Space Walk
   195→
   196→### Polarity-Encoded Addresses
   197→
   198→Literal addresses encode BOTH variable AND polarity via
   199→`Literal.toNat`:
   200→
   201→  `toNat lit = 2 * lit.particle_idx.val +
   202→    (if lit.polarity then 1 else 0)`
   203→
   204→This gives **2k unique addresses** (linear in k, NOT exponential).
   205→
   206→### Walk Structure
   207→
   208→For each clause in the CNF, the walk records the polarity-encoded
   209→EntropyNat addresses of ALL literals in that clause.
   210→
   211→  walk cost <= |cnf| x k x 2k = 2 x |cnf| x k^2
   212→
   213→This is polynomial in the input size n = |encodeCNF cnf|.
   214→-/
   215→
   216→/--
   217→**Polarity-encoded literal address.**
   218→
   219→Maps each literal to a unique N address encoding both variable
   220→position AND polarity. For k variables, there are 2k addresses:
   221→{0, 1, ..., 2k-1}.
   222→
   223→- `(x_i, true)`  -> `2i + 1` (odd addresses = positive polarity)
   224→- `(x_i, false)` -> `2i`    (even addresses = negative polarity)
   225→
   226→This is the existing `Literal.toNat` from CNF.lean.
   227→-/
   228→def literalAddress {k : ℕ} (lit : Literal k) : ℕ :=
   229→  Literal.toNat lit
   230→
   231→/--
   232→**Literal address as an EntropyNat.**
   233→
   234→Each literal address `n` maps to `ofNat n = replicate n true` —
   235→an EntropyNat of length `n`. The walk records these addresses.
   236→-/
   237→def literalAddressPath {k : ℕ} (lit : Literal k) :
   238→    EntropyNat :=
   239→  EntropyNat.ofNat (literalAddress lit)
   240→
   241→/--
   242→**Each literal address is bounded by 2k.**
   243→
   244→Since `lit.particle_idx : Fin k`, we have
   245→`lit.particle_idx.val < k`, so
   246→`literalAddress lit = 2 * lit.particle_idx.val + (0 or 1) < 2k`.
   247→-/
   248→theorem literalAddress_lt_two_k {k : ℕ}
   249→    (lit : Literal k) :
   250→    literalAddress lit < 2 * k := by
   251→  simp only [literalAddress, Literal.toNat]
   252→  have h := lit.particle_idx.isLt
   253→  by_cases hp : lit.polarity <;> simp [hp] <;> omega
   254→
   255→/--
   256→**NDM address-space walk: endpoint-free clause-by-clause address
   257→recording.**
   258→
   259→For each clause in the CNF, records the EntropyNat addresses of ALL
   260→literals in that clause. No endpoint parameter. The walk processes
   261→all clauses and records the complete polarity-encoded address
   262→structure.
   263→
   264→The output is `List (List EntropyNat)` — one list of addresses per
   265→clause.
   266→-/
   267→def ndmAddressWalk {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   268→    List (List EntropyNat) :=
   269→  cnf.map (fun clause => clause.map literalAddressPath)
   270→
   271→/--
   272→**NDM walk complexity: total EntropyNat address cost.**
   273→
   274→The complexity is the sum of all literal address values across all
   275→clauses. Each address value =
   276→`toNat (literalAddressPath lit)` = `literalAddress lit`.
   277→-/
   278→def ndmWalkComplexity {k : ℕ}
   279→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) : ℕ :=
   280→  ((ndmAddressWalk cnf).map
   281→    (fun paths =>
   282→      (paths.map EntropyNat.toNat).sum)).sum
   283→
   284→/--
   285→**Per-clause address cost is bounded by |clause| x 2k.**
   286→
   287→Each literal address < 2k, so the sum of addresses in a clause
   288→with m literals is < m x 2k.
   289→-/
   290→theorem clause_address_cost_le {k : ℕ}
   291→    (clause : Clause k) :
   292→    ((clause.map literalAddressPath).map
   293→      EntropyNat.toNat).sum ≤
   294→        clause.length * (2 * k) := by
   295→  rw [List.map_map]
   296→  apply sum_map_le_length_mul_bound
   297→  intro lit h_mem
   298→  simp only [Function.comp]
   299→  simp only [literalAddressPath,
   300→    EntropyNat.ofNat_toNat]
   301→  exact Nat.le_of_lt (literalAddress_lt_two_k lit)
   302→
   303→/--
   304→**NDM walk complexity is polynomial: bounded by
   305→|cnf| x k x 2k.**
   306→
   307→Total cost = sum over clauses of (sum of literal addresses in
   308→clause). Each clause has <= k literals, each literal address < 2k.
   309→So total <= |cnf| x k x 2k = 2 x |cnf| x k^2.
   310→
   311→This is polynomial in n = |encodeCNF cnf| (since |cnf| <= n and
   312→k <= n).
   313→-/
   314→theorem ndmWalkComplexity_polynomial {k : ℕ}
   315→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   316→    (h_clause_bound : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c.length ≤ k) :
   317→    ndmWalkComplexity cnf ≤
   318→      cnf.length * (k * (2 * k)) := by
   319→  unfold ndmWalkComplexity ndmAddressWalk
   320→  simp only [List.map_map]
   321→  induction cnf with
   322→  | nil => simp
   323→  | cons head tail ih =>
   324→    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons,
   325→      List.length_cons]
   326→    have h_head_bound : head.length ≤ k :=
   327→      h_clause_bound head
   328→        (List.mem_cons.mpr (Or.inl rfl))
   329→    have h_tail_bound : ∀ c ∈ tail, c.length ≤ k :=
   330→      fun c hc => h_clause_bound c
   331→        (List.mem_cons.mpr (Or.inr hc))
   332→    have h_head_le := clause_address_cost_le head
   333→    have h_mul_le := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (2 * k) h_head_bound
   334→    have h_head_cost :
   335→        ((head.map literalAddressPath).map EntropyNat.toNat).sum
   336→          ≤ k * (2 * k) := by linarith
   337→    have h_tail_cost := ih h_tail_bound
   338→    simp only [Function.comp, List.map_map] at h_head_cost h_tail_cost ⊢
   339→    linarith
   340→
   341→/-!
   342→### NDM Entropy Walk: Conditional Entropy Inside the Machine
   343→
   344→The NDM entropy walk INTERNALIZES the conditional entropy
   345→decomposition: the walk machine carries the conditional entropy
   346→accumulator as it processes clauses. At each clause, the walk
   347→simultaneously:
   348→
   349→1. Records literal addresses (the `ndmAddressWalk` component)
   350→2. Computes the conditional clause entropy (the chain rule
   351→   component)
   352→3. Accumulates the total entropy (the SAT-determination component)
   353→-/
   354→
   355→/-- State of the NDM entropy walk: carries the walk's address record
   356→    alongside the conditional entropy accumulation. -/
   357→structure NDMEntropyWalkState (k : ℕ) where
   358→  /-- The composite being tested (encodes the variable
   359→  assignment) -/
   360→  composite : ℕ
   361→  /-- Running total of conditional entropy across processed
   362→  clauses -/
   363→  totalEntropy : ℝ
   364→  /-- Per-clause conditional entropy contributions (chain rule
   365→  terms) -/
   366→  clauseEntropies : List ℝ
   367→  /-- Literal addresses recorded per clause (the ndmAddressWalk
   368→  component) -/
   369→  addressRecord : List (List EntropyNat)
   370→
   371→/-- Initialize the entropy walk state with a composite. -/
   372→noncomputable def NDMEntropyWalkState.init {k : ℕ}
   373→    (composite : ℕ) :
   374→    NDMEntropyWalkState k :=
   375→  { composite := composite
   376→    totalEntropy := 0
   377→    clauseEntropies := []
   378→    addressRecord := [] }
   379→
   380→/--
   381→One step of the NDM entropy walk: process a single clause.
   382→
   383→Simultaneously:
   384→1. Records the clause's literal addresses (address walk component)
   385→2. Computes `conditionalClauseEntropy composite clause`
   386→   (entropy component)
   387→3. Adds the clause entropy to the running total (chain rule
   388→   accumulation)
   389→-/
   390→noncomputable def ndmEntropyStep {k : ℕ}
   391→    (clause : Clause k)
   392→    (state : NDMEntropyWalkState k) :
   393→    NDMEntropyWalkState k :=
   394→  let clauseAddresses := clause.map literalAddressPath
   395→  let clauseH :=
   396→    conditionalClauseEntropy state.composite clause
   397→  { state with
   398→    totalEntropy := state.totalEntropy + clauseH
   399→    clauseEntropies :=
   400→      state.clauseEntropies ++ [clauseH]
   401→    addressRecord :=
   402→      state.addressRecord ++ [clauseAddresses] }
   403→
   404→/--
   405→The full NDM entropy walk: process all clauses sequentially.
   406→
   407→The walk folds over the CNF clause by clause, simultaneously
   408→recording literal addresses and accumulating conditional entropy.
   409→-/
   410→noncomputable def ndmEntropyWalk {k : ℕ}
   411→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   412→    (composite : ℕ) : NDMEntropyWalkState k :=
   413→  cnf.foldl
   414→    (fun state clause => ndmEntropyStep clause state)
   415→    (NDMEntropyWalkState.init composite)
   416→
   417→/-- The composite field is preserved by ndmEntropyStep. -/
   418→private theorem ndmEntropyStep_composite {k : ℕ}
   419→    (clause : Clause k)
   420→    (state : NDMEntropyWalkState k) :
   421→    (ndmEntropyStep clause state).composite =
   422→      state.composite := by
   423→  simp [ndmEntropyStep]
   424→
   425→/-- The composite field is preserved by the full foldl walk. -/
   426→private theorem ndmEntropyWalk_foldl_composite {k : ℕ}
   427→    (cnf : List (Clause k))
   428→    (init : NDMEntropyWalkState k) :
   429→    (cnf.foldl
   430→      (fun state clause =>
   431→        ndmEntropyStep clause state) init).composite =
   432→      init.composite := by
   433→  induction cnf generalizing init with
   434→  | nil => simp
   435→  | cons head tail ih =>
   436→    simp only [List.foldl_cons]
   437→    rw [ih, ndmEntropyStep_composite]
   438→
   439→/-- Helper: the foldl accumulation pattern for totalEntropy. -/
   440→private theorem ndmEntropyWalk_foldl_total {k : ℕ}
   441→    (cnf : List (Clause k))
   442→    (init : NDMEntropyWalkState k) :
   443→    (cnf.foldl
   444→      (fun state clause =>
   445→        ndmEntropyStep clause state)
   446→          init).totalEntropy =
   447→      init.totalEntropy +
   448→        (cnf.map
   449→          (conditionalClauseEntropy
   450→            init.composite)).sum := by
   451→  induction cnf generalizing init with
   452→  | nil => simp
   453→  | cons head tail ih =>
   454→    simp only [List.foldl_cons, List.map_cons,
   455→      List.sum_cons]
   456→    rw [ih]
   457→    simp only [ndmEntropyStep,
   458→      ndmEntropyStep_composite]
   459→    ring
   460→
   461→/--
   462→**The entropy walk's total equals the conditional CNF entropy.**
   463→
   464→The walk accumulates exactly
   465→`conditionalCNFEntropy composite cnf`: each clause step adds
   466→`conditionalClauseEntropy composite clause` to the running total,
   467→and the sum is the conditional CNF entropy.
   468→-/
   469→theorem ndmEntropyWalk_total_eq {k : ℕ}
   470→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   471→    (composite : ℕ) :
   472→    (ndmEntropyWalk cnf composite).totalEntropy =
   473→      conditionalCNFEntropy composite cnf := by
   474→  unfold ndmEntropyWalk
   475→  rw [ndmEntropyWalk_foldl_total]
   476→  simp [NDMEntropyWalkState.init,
   477→    conditionalCNFEntropy]
   478→
   479→/--
   480→**The entropy walk determines SAT.**
   481→
   482→The NDM entropy walk's total entropy is zero iff the CNF is
   483→satisfiable under the assignment encoded by the composite.
   484→-/
   485→theorem ndmEntropyWalk_determines_sat {k : ℕ}
   486→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   487→    (a : Vector Bool k)
   488→    (h_clauses_nonempty : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c ≠ []) :
   489→    (ndmEntropyWalk cnf
   490→      (assignmentCompositePrime a)).totalEntropy = 0 ↔
   491→      evalCNF cnf a = true := by
   492→  rw [ndmEntropyWalk_total_eq]
   493→  exact (cnfSharesFactor_iff_zero_conditional_cnf_entropy
   494→    a cnf h_clauses_nonempty).symm.trans
   495→    (evalCNF_true_iff_cnfSharesFactor a cnf).symm
   496→
   497→/-- Helper: the foldl accumulation pattern for
   498→addressRecord. -/
   499→private theorem ndmEntropyWalk_foldl_addressRecord
   500→    {k : ℕ}
   501→    (cnf : List (Clause k))
   502→    (init : NDMEntropyWalkState k) :
   503→    (cnf.foldl
   504→      (fun state clause =>
   505→        ndmEntropyStep clause state)
   506→          init).addressRecord =
   507→      init.addressRecord ++
   508→        cnf.map (fun clause =>
   509→          clause.map literalAddressPath) := by
   510→  induction cnf generalizing init with
   511→  | nil => simp
   512→  | cons head tail ih =>
   513→    simp only [List.foldl_cons, List.map_cons]

   536→      (ndmEntropyWalk cnf
   537→        (assignmentCompositePrime a)).totalEntropy =
   538→          0) ↔
   539→      (∃ a : Vector Bool k,
   540→        evalCNF cnf a = true) := by

   559→      (fun state clause =>

   562→      init.clauseEntropies.length + cnf.length := by

   583→/-! ## Circuit SAT via NDM Address Space
   584→
   585→### The Key Insight
   586→
   587→The NDM circuit model:
   588→- INPUTS: the variable literal addresses (2k total, k selected by
   589→  any assignment)
   590→- CONSTRAINTS: the CNF clauses (each clause specifies which literal
   591→  addresses satisfy it)
   592→- OUTPUT: whether the selected input addresses are consistent with
   593→  all constraints
   594→
   595→### Architecture
   596→
   597→1. `literalAddressesFromAssignment` — the k addresses selected by
   598→   assignment a
   599→2. `ndmCircuitEval` — circuit evaluation in address space
   600→3. `ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF` — the NDM circuit IS evalCNF
   601→   (capstone)
   602→4. Polynomial cost properties
   603→-/
   604→
   605→/--
   606→**The addresses selected by an assignment.**
   607→
   608→For each variable index i, the assignment selects the literal
   609→`chosenLiteral a i`, and its address is
   610→`literalAddress (chosenLiteral a i)`. This gives exactly k literal
   611→addresses.
   612→-/
   613→def literalAddressesFromAssignment {k : ℕ}
   614→    (a : Vector Bool k) : Finset ℕ :=
   615→  Finset.image
   616→    (fun i => literalAddress (chosenLiteral a i))
   617→    Finset.univ
   618→
   619→/--
   620→**The fundamental bridge: `evalLiteral lit a = true` iff
   621→`literalAddress lit ∈ literalAddressesFromAssignment a`.**
   622→-/
   623→theorem evalLiteral_iff_mem_literalAddresses {k : ℕ}
   624→    (lit : Literal k)
   625→    (a : Vector Bool k) :
   626→    evalLiteral lit a = true ↔
   627→      literalAddress lit ∈
   628→        literalAddressesFromAssignment a := by
   629→  constructor
   630→  · intro h_eval
   631→    have h_pol :=
   632→      (evalLiteral_eq_true_iff_polarity_eq lit a).mp
   633→        h_eval
   634→    simp only [literalAddressesFromAssignment,
   635→      Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   636→    refine ⟨lit.particle_idx, ?_⟩
   637→    -- literalAddress lit =
   638→    --   literalAddress (chosenLiteral a lit.particle_idx)
   639→    -- Since lit.polarity = a.get lit.particle_idx,
   640→    -- the chosen literal matches
   641→    unfold literalAddress chosenLiteral
   642→    simp only [Literal.toNat, h_pol]
   643→  · intro h_mem
   644→    simp only [literalAddressesFromAssignment,
   645→      Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ,
   646→      true_and] at h_mem
   647→    rcases h_mem with ⟨i, h_addr_eq⟩
   648→    -- h_addr_eq : literalAddress lit =
   649→    --   literalAddress (chosenLiteral a i)
   650→    unfold literalAddress chosenLiteral at h_addr_eq
   651→    simp only [Literal.toNat] at h_addr_eq
   652→    rw [evalLiteral_eq_true_iff_polarity_eq]
   653→    -- From h_addr_eq, extract idx equality and polarity
   654→    -- equality
   655→    have h_idx_val :
   656→        lit.particle_idx.val = i.val := by
   657→      -- h_addr_eq involves `if` expressions;
   658→      -- case-split to enable omega
   659→      cases hp : lit.polarity <;>
   660→        cases ha : (a.get i) <;>
   661→        simp [hp, ha] at h_addr_eq <;> omega
   662→    have h_idx : lit.particle_idx = i :=
   663→      Fin.ext h_idx_val
   664→    subst h_idx
   665→    -- Now h_addr_eq gives polarity match
   666→    cases h_pol : lit.polarity <;>
   667→      cases h_val : (a.get lit.particle_idx) <;>
   668→      simp_all
   669→
   670→/--
   671→**The NDM circuit: given an assignment's literal addresses and a
   672→CNF, check if every clause contains at least one selected
   673→address.**
   674→
   675→This operates entirely in address space — no direct reference to
   676→the assignment vector, only to the addresses it selects.
   677→-/
   678→def ndmCircuitEval {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   679→    (a : Vector Bool k) : Bool :=
   680→  cnf.all (fun clause => clause.any (fun lit =>
   681→    decide (literalAddress lit ∈
   682→      literalAddressesFromAssignment a)))
   683→
   684→/--
   685→**The NDM circuit evaluation equals `evalCNF`.**
   686→
   687→This is the capstone theorem: the NDM circuit IS evalCNF, operating
   688→entirely in address space.
   689→-/
   690→theorem ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF {k : ℕ}
   691→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   692→    (a : Vector Bool k) :
   693→    ndmCircuitEval cnf a = evalCNF cnf a := by
   694→  simp only [ndmCircuitEval, evalCNF, evalClause]
   695→  congr 1
   696→  ext clause
   697→  congr 1
   698→  ext lit
   699→  cases h : evalLiteral lit a
   700→  · simp only [decide_eq_false_iff_not]
   701→    intro h_mem
   702→    have :=
   703→      (evalLiteral_iff_mem_literalAddresses lit a).mpr
   704→        h_mem
   705→    rw [h] at this
   706→    exact absurd this Bool.noConfusion
   707→  · simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]
   708→    exact (evalLiteral_iff_mem_literalAddresses
   709→      lit a).mp h
   710→
   711→/--
   712→**The NDM circuit cost is polynomial: O(|cnf| x k).**
   713→-/
   714→theorem ndmCircuit_cost_polynomial {k : ℕ}
   715→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   716→    (h_clause_bound : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c.length ≤ k) :
   717→    (cnf.map (fun c => c.length)).sum ≤
   718→      cnf.length * k := by
   719→  apply sum_map_le_length_mul_bound
   720→  exact h_clause_bound
   721→
   722→/--
   723→**Entropy bridge: NDM circuit evaluation matches the entropy walk
   724→determination.**
   725→
   726→`ndmCircuitEval cnf a = true ↔
   727→  ndmEntropyWalk(composite).totalEntropy = 0`.
   728→-/
   729→theorem ndmCircuit_entropy_bridge {k : ℕ}
   730→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   731→    (a : Vector Bool k)
   732→    (h_clauses_nonempty : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c ≠ []) :
   733→    ndmCircuitEval cnf a = true ↔
   734→      (ndmEntropyWalk cnf
   735→        (assignmentCompositePrime a)).totalEntropy =
   736→          0 := by
   737→  rw [ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF]
   738→  exact (ndmEntropyWalk_determines_sat cnf a
   739→    h_clauses_nonempty).symm
   740→
   741→/--
   742→**SAT iff exists assignment where the NDM circuit accepts.**
   743→-/
   744→theorem ndmCircuit_sat_iff {k : ℕ}
   745→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   746→    (∃ a : Vector Bool k,
   747→      ndmCircuitEval cnf a = true) ↔
   748→    (∃ a : Vector Bool k,
   749→      evalCNF cnf a = true) := by
   750→  constructor
   751→  · rintro ⟨a, h⟩
   752→    exact ⟨a, (ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF cnf a) ▸ h⟩
   753→  · rintro ⟨a, h⟩
   754→    exact ⟨a, (ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF cnf a) ▸ h⟩
   755→
   756→end InformationTheory

   607→least one literal in the clause has zero conditional entropy
   608→(shares a factor). A clause is satisfied iff some literal
   609→contributes no new information.

   612→    (composite : ℕ) (clause : Clause k) : ℝ :=
